content:
If the account is IMAP, nothing will be lost. If POP then, I suggest doing this first:

  1. install the addon, importexporttools NG
  2. highlight the inbox, rightclick and select the importexport option to export mbox
  3. repeat for sent folder

On old drive,

  1. locate the c:\users\<yourid>\appdata\roaming\thunderbird folder and copy to external media

On new PC, do this:

  1. ensure thunderbird is installed, run once, and NOT running
  2. enter %appdata% in search window on task bar and press Enter key
  3. delete the thunderbird folder
  4. you should be in Appdata\roaming folder , copy&paste the exported Thunderbird folder there. This is a 100% replacement
  5. start thunderbird and all should be there except the exported POP messages

IF POP, these are final steps: With the importexport addon installed

  1. highlight the POP inbox, rightclick and select the importexport option to impor mbox and import the file you saved
  2. repeat for sent folder

Well, OK, you answered one out of three questions - I guess that's a step in the right direction...

Who is your email provider (Gmail, Yahoo, Comcast, Outlook, AOL, etc.)?

After you install the program and run it for the first time, you will be prompted to set up an email account in Thunderbird for your email provider. You will need to know, at a minimum, your current email address. If it's with a common email provider that might be enough for Thunderbird to find the proper server settings and set things up for you. This article describes the automatic set up process:

https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/automatic-account-configuration

If it's a less well-know provider, you might need to look up the server settings on the provider's web site, and then set up the account manually.

https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/manual-account-configuration
